item: exclusive_window's finally raises the paused flag itself, so an interrupt between the pause's report and the body still resumes collection
refs: Q's yes and exact shape (coordinator 17 Oct); the gap was found by the reader of #1431 (C6)
summary: exclusive_window set _EXCL_PAUSED only inside the body's with _EXCL_LOCK, so an interrupt delivered after pause_for_exclusive_operation returned True and before that body ran left collection stopped, while the comment said that could only happen before the pause reported. With a C lock the gap is practically unreachable; with a Python-level lock wrapper (how the test file models an interrupt) it is reachable and the reader's probe ran (collection not restarted, starts 0). The finally now raises the flag when was_paused is set, inside _EXCL_LOCK and before the depth and the resume decision; idempotent with the body's own line. The residual is named in the comment: an interrupt between the pause call returning and the was_paused store still finds nothing to resume (the Start button puts it right). tests/test_exclusive_window_interrupt_safe.py gains the probe: red without the change (collection stopped, starts 0), green with it.
